MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  June 13, 2023
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Goodell at
5:00 p.m., on June 13, 2023, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on June 8, 2023, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at the
Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Ruesch
  Council Member Vasquez
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Goodell

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Labor Negotiations - The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957 and 54957.6. The Parties to the
  Negotiations Are the City and City’s Unrepresented Employees. The City’s Negotiator
  is Dennis Wilberg.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE
At the hour of 5:01 pm, Mayor Goodell recessed to Closed Session. The City Council reconvened
at 6:00 pm with all five City Council Members.

City Council Minutes  1  June 13, 2023
 REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

Assistant City Attorney John Harper announced that there was one closed session item but there was
no reportable action.

INVOCATION: Bishop Dunn of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Ruesch

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Presentation by City of Hope Orange County

  Received presentation from Director of Strategic Initiatives Alana Gebhart.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS (taken out of order)

29. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) Report

  Received report from Capital Projects Outreach Section Manager Chris Boucly.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Sara Mehrmand, Trabuco Canyon: Spoke in favor of Item 18 regarding the fencing at Napoli Park
and outlined her reasons why this is a good idea.

Adam Chrisape, Rancho Santa Margarita: Introduced himself as a representative on behalf of
Assemblywoman Kate Sanchez and spoke on various upcoming events she will be holding.

Stacy Holmes, MV: Stated that he attended and learned a lot from the photographic and historic
presentation from the Heritage Committee. He pointed out a couple of Commissioner Breton’s
presentation points regarding population increases through the years and the goals of the Mission
Viejo Company to attract buyers from all social strata, economic backgrounds and walks of life. He
asked that the City Council honor our history as we put together the Housing Element.

Cathy Palmer, MV: She raised concerns that two individuals that have spoken on the record
regarding the Core Vision Plan did not identify their relationship with the City. She voiced that she
supports the Core Vision Plan if it was a mixed-use development and questioned the new commercial
development on Alicia Parkway by Target that should be watched closely for the success or failure
for franchises in order to generate tax revenue.

Lori Young, MV: Stated that she attended the rally on the corner of Marguerite and La Paz the first
Saturday of June to celebrate Pride Month and to show her support for the LGBTQ+ community.
She thanked Council Member Vasquez for stopping by an showing her support.

City Council Minutes  2  June 13, 2023
 CONSENT CALENDAR

Item #18 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of May 23, 2023, as presented.

2.  General Check Register Dated May 12, 2023 in the Amount of $686,938.19

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  General Check Register Dated May 19, 2023 in the Amount of $963,860.59

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  General Check Register Dated May 26, 2023 in the Amount of $1,633,024.41

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Golf Check Register Dated May 12, 2023 in the Amount of $23,531.96

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  Golf Check Register Dated May 19, 2023 in the Amount of $4,630.67

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

7.  Golf Check Register Dated May 26, 2023 in the Amount of $78,597.20

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

8.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for April 2023

  Received and filed.
City Council Minutes  3  June 13, 2023
 9.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report
  for April 2023

  Received and filed.

10. Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for April 2023

  Received and filed.

11. Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for April 2023

  Received and filed.

12. Purchase of Two Replacement Servers for City Data Center

  Approved purchase order to Dell Marketing LP in amount not to exceed $40,578.33 for
  purchase of two PowerEdge R760 servers for the City's primary datacenter.

13. Professional Services Agreement for Printing and Related Services for the "Mission Viejo
  Life" Publication

  (1) Approved the Professional Services Agreement with Advantage Inc. (A23-25) for printing
  and related services for up to eight issues of Mission Viejo Life in the amount of $174,667.92
  for the period of July 1, 2023, through June 30, 2025; and (2) authorized issuance of a purchase
  order to Advantage Inc. for the period of July 1, 2023, through June 30, 2024, in an amount
  not to exceed $86,733.96.

14. 2023 Fourth of July Community Street Faire

  Approved the Special Events Permit submitted by the Mission Viejo Activities Committee
  authorizing the annual Mission Viejo Fourth of July Community Street Faire on Tuesday, July
  4, 2023.

15. 2023 Local Traffic Signal Synchronization Plan (LSSP) Update for Measure M2 Funding
  Eligibility

  Adopted Resolution 23-20 Concerning the 2023 Update for the Local Signal Synchronization
  Plan in order to maintain eligibility for funding through the Orange County Measure M (M2)
  Program.

City Council Minutes  4  June 13, 2023
 16. Maintenance of Traffic Signals and Appurtenance, Interconnect, Battery Back-Up
  Systems, Illuminated Street Name Signs, Safety Lights, CCTV Cameras, Speed Feedback
  Signs and Illuminated Crosswalks-Award of Contract

  (1) Awarded the contract for the subject services to Bear Electrical Solutions (BES) (A23-26)
  for the period July 1, 2023, to June 30, 2025, in the amount of $920,000; and (2) authorized
  issuance of a purchase order to BES for the period July 1, 2023, to June 30, 2024, in an amount
  not to exceed $460,000.

17. Annual Weed Abatement Program for Parcels Under One Acre - Year 2023 - Phase 1

  (1) Adopted Resolution 23-21 Declaring that Certain Weeds, Rubbish, Refuse, and Dirt on
  Parcels Under One Acre Constitute Nuisances; Declaring the Intention of the City Council to
  Order the Abatement of Said Nuisances; and Fixing a Time and Place for Hearing Protests; (2)
  instructed the Public Services Department to mail a Notice to Destroy Weeds in accordance
  with Section 39566 of the Government Code; and (3) instructed the City Clerk to set the Public
  Hearing for August 22, 2023.

19. Annual Maintenance Program for Electrical and Related Services at All City Facilities

  (1) Awarded a contract to David Electric, Inc. (A23-27) for Annual Routine Electrical and
  Related Services for the period of July 1, 2023 to June 30, 2025 in an amount not to exceed
  $438,000.00; and (2) authorized the issuance of a purchase order to David Electric, Inc. for the
  period July 1, 2023 to June 30, 2024, in amount not to exceed $338,000.00, pending adoption
  of the Fiscal Year 2023-2025 budget by the City Council.

20. Annual Maintenance Program for Heating, Ventilation and Air-Conditioning Related
  Services at City Facilities

  (1) Awarded a contract to South Coast Mechanical, LLC (A23-28)for Annual Routine HVAC
  and Related Services for the period of July 1, 2023 to June 30, 2025 in an amount not to exceed
  $240,000; and (2) authorized the issuance of a purchase order to South Coast Mechanical, LLC
  for the period July 1, 2023 to June 30, 2024, in amount not to exceed $120,000.00, pending
  adoption of the Fiscal Year 2023-2025 budget by the City Council.

21. Annual Routine Janitorial and Related Services at City Facilities

  (1) Approved Tenth Amendment to the existing maintenance contract with Alliance Building
  Maintenance, LLC for the subject services for the period of July 1, 2023 through June 30, 2025
  in the amount of $1,446,794.00; and (2) authorized issuance of a purchase order to Alliance
  Building Maintenance, LLC for the period of July 1, 2023 through June 30, 2024, in an amount
  not to exceed $723,397.00 pending adoption of the 2023-2025 budget by City Council.

City Council Minutes  5  June 13, 2023
 22. Annual Routine Janitorial Supplies at City Facilities

  Authorized staff to issue a purchase order to Waxie Sanitary Supply for Janitorial Supplies at
  City Facilities for the period of July 1, 2023 to May 31, 2024 in the amount of $140,000.00,
  pending adoption of the Fiscal Year 2023-2025 budget by the City Council.

23. Animal Services Service Agreement with the City of Laguna Niguel

  Approved the Agreement for Animal Control and Shelter Services with the City of Laguna
  Niguel (A23-29).

24. Animal Services Service Agreement with the City of Aliso Viejo

  Approved the Agreement for Animal Control and Shelter Services with the City of Aliso Viejo
  (A23-30).

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

18. General Fence Maintenance - Installation of Fencing at Napoli Park

  Director of Public Services Jerry Hill presented the staff report.

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley suggested that this item be postponed until an outreach has been
  conducted with other schools in the City that are next to city parks.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Vasquez, (1)
  approve Second Amendment to JM Justus Fence Company (A23-31B) for the subject services
  for the period of May 23, 2023 through September 30, 2023 to increase the contract by an
  amount not to exceed $75,000.00, (2) authorize issuance of a Change Order to JM Justus Fence
  Company in the amount not to exceed $75,000.00, and (3) to fence only the three sides where
  the slopes are located and to look at other parks that are adjacent to schools.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

25. Banking Services

  Administrative Services Manager Susan Knudson presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to adopt (1)
  Approved the selection of U.S. Bank (A23-32) to provide banking services to the City of
City Council Minutes  6  June 13, 2023
   Mission Viejo for the five-year period July 1, 2023 through June 30, 2028 and authorize the
  City Manager to execute the agreement; and (2) the Mission Viejo Housing Authority Board
  approved the selection of U.S. Bank to provide banking services to the Mission Viejo Housing
  Authority for the five-year period July 1, 2023 through June 30, 2028 and authorized the
  Executive Director to execute the agreement; and (3) the Successor Agency of the Community
  Development Agency of the City of Mission Viejo approved the selection of U.S. Bank to
  provide banking services to the Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency
  for the five-year period July 1, 2023 through June 30, 2028 and authorize staff to execute the
  agreement.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

26. Review of 2023-25 Proposed Budget

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Council Members made comments and asked questions of staff regarding the budget.

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley specifically asked that if there is a surplus this fiscal year that we
  consider park renovations back in the budget.

  Council Member Vasquez specifically asked that the OakHouse Church lease be noted in the
  budget. She asked for a discussion on the prioritization on the strategic goals and how these
  projects will be paid.

  Mayor Goodell explained that studies are being currently being done such as the Core Vision
  Plan and once that process is finished it will determine what the cost will be and then how it
  will be funded. He stated it is pretty much the same answer for the Oso Creek Parking Garage,
  Lower Curtis Park, and the Community Theater.

  Director Dyas suggested that in order to find a consensus after the completion of the two
  current feasibility studies to develop an objective under the City Council Department to have
  a conversation about prioritizing projects including the parking structure, the theater, core area
  vision plan, and annual playground renovations. She stressed that this will help Staff as to a
  clear prioritization agreed among the Council.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ruesch, to (1) direct
  staff to place the 2023-25 proposed budget on the June 27, 2023 City Council agenda for
  adoption; and (4) adopt Resolution 23-22 Amending the Authorized Position Schedule
  effective July 1, 2023.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  7  June 13, 2023
   AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS (Continued)

27. Transportation Corridor Agencies (TCA) Report

  Received report from Mayor Pro Tem Kelley.

28. Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  Received report from Council Member Bucknum.

29. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) Report

  Received report from Mayor Goodell.

CITY MANAGER REPORTS

30. Residential Parking Issues - Aprico Drive

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report.

  By consensus the City Council received and filed the report.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

31. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

 Council Member Bucknum

 Council Member Bucknum attended the following events: The Grapes and Grains at Norman P.
 Murray Center, the AYSO Mission Viejo Classic at the Oso Viejo Park, and the Chamber of
 Commerce Annual Breakfast. She gave an update on the Sober Living Task Force and shared an
 article from the Orange County Register regarding regulations of Sober Living Homes. She
 encouraged residents to sign up for updates on the task force website

City Council Minutes  8  June 13, 2023
  www.soberlivingtaskforce.com She announced that the next meeting will be at Laguna Niguel City
 Hall on July 14 at 2 pm. She spoke on backyard hens and it is her understanding that there is an
 ordinance in place that does allow for a small number of hens that will require a permitting process
 with the Animal Services Department. She stressed that this only applies to hens not roosters and
 that your homeowner’s association will also have to approve. Council Member Bucknum suggested
 if it’s possible to use farm animals for weed abatement. Lastly, she encouraged the residents to
 attend the annual Street Faire on the 4th of July.

 Council Member Ruesch

 Council Member Ruesch announced he attended the closing ceremonies of the Little League, the
 AYSO Mission Viejo Classic, Chamber Breakfast, and stated he has been having coffee with former
 Mayors. He concluded he and Aliso Viejo Council Ross Chung toured the City on an OCFA
 helicopter to view fire vulnerability particularly on the eastern border of the City and encouraged
 fire mitigation for those that butts up against this border to create defensible spaces.

 Council Member Vasquez

 Council Member Vasquez attended the Memorial Day Ceremony in the Kershaw Garden and stated
 that it was very well attended. She also attended the Bathgate Elementary Character Awards and
 attended the CJPIA Conference for new elected officials in Huntington Beach. Council Member
 Vasquez announced that her oldest daughter is learning how to drive and that her youngest daughter
 bridged to Brownies this past weekend.
 Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

 Mayor Pro Tem Kelley gave a shout-out to Director of Recreation & Community Services Mark Nix
 and Leslie McDonald for the fantastic Memorial Day Ceremony. She indicated that it was a very
 moving ceremony and she read an excerpt from an email from former Mayor Rhonda Reardon. She
 stated that she also attended the AYSO Mission Viejo Classic. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley gave a shout-
 out to the volunteers of The Friends of the Library Book Store on the recent Book Sale that raised a
 lot of money. She thanked the Mission Viejo Activities Committee for the upcoming Fourth of July
 Street Faire. She gave kudos to Executive Director Michelle Mitchell on her amazing job with the
 Nadadores Team and Foundation. She noted that Michelle is bringing the 2023 Diving Junior
 Nationals Championships to Mission Viejo on July 22.

 Mayor Goodell

 Mayor Goodell attended a Gala in Los Angeles celebrating sports diplomacy, global policy in the
 2028 Olympics and Paralympics in an effort to bring Olympic Teams here to train. He also attended
 the Orange County Council of Governments Board of Directors Meeting along with the Executive
 Board Meeting; the Memorial Day Service here in the City as well as at the El Toro Memorial Park,
 and the Little League Closing Ceremonies. Mayor Goodell announced that he attended a coffee and
 conversation with Supervisor Katrina Foley in Rancho Mission Viejo last week regarding fire
 protection, fire codes, and the fire maps. He stated this is a big issue with Insurance companies such
 as State Farm who is no longer writing home owner policies in the whole State of California. He was
 told that the best bet is to go with Travelers Insurance. Mayor Goodell also attended the Chamber
 Breakfast. He stated the Diving Meet will be a huge economic generator for our City predicting well
 over a million dollars being spent in our City. He announced that tomorrow at 3 pm will be the second
City Council Minutes  9  June 13, 2023
  ad hoc committee meeting of the Olympic Sports Promotion Committee here in the Council Chamber
 to discuss bringing teams here to train. He stated that Michelle Mitchell has contact with the US
 Association of Triathlons who have interest in hosting the world championships in Mission Viejo for
 the next three to five years, as well as the college triathlon championships. There is also talks with
 FIFA to get soccer teams to train here for the World Cup. He concluded that there is a lot going on
 and there is a buzz in the sports world with the 2028 Olympics coming to Los Angeles.

 ADJOURNMENT

 At the hour of 9:30 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
 Mayor Goodell adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, June 27, 2023, at 5:00 p.m.

 ______________________________________
 Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of June 27, 2023

City Council Minutes  10  June 13, 2023
